scope: Theorem 2.2 (Local estimate with variation in depth) of the manuscript “Triple ergodic averages with distinct integer slopes” (preprints/Triple-ergodic-averages-with-distinct-integer-slopes-October-4-2026/triple-ergodic-distinct-slopes.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 154 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 883a45bc7b95cfaf), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 3-4. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix the primitive distinct integers b0 = 0, b1, b2, b3 and the parameters δ0, C0. Let T be a finite dyadic tree with root J and largest depth d, and let I ⊆ T . Assign an admissible kernel to every I ∈ I. For each 0 ≤ j ≤ 3, let zj,s : J → C, 0 ≤ s ≤ d, be measurable, and partition {0, . . . , d} into Wj ≥ 1 deterministic nonempty consecutive blocks. Suppose that VB(zj) ≤ W −1/2 j almost everywhere on J 4 OPENAI for each block in the jth partition. Extend every input by zero outside J. Then (2.4) X I∈I |I| |HI(z0,s(I), z1,s(I), z2,s(I), z3,s(I))| ≤ Cb,δ0,C0 |J|. The constant is independent of the lattice, tree, depth range, subcollection, kernels, and the four partitions and their sizes.
